#list-item in Figma

tap or drag the component: the right side shows what happens in the app

One row of a list, Material 3's list item, with a leading icon or image, a headline, supporting text and a trailing end; rows live in a ListView.

Put it on a screen

  1. Assets → the library → drag #list-item onto the screen and pick any variant (the app sets the real one).
  2. Wrap it in a frame (Ctrl/Cmd + Alt + G) of the same size and name the frame SLOT: that name is the contract with the app. A list is a clipping frame with as many preview rows as it shows; the scrollbar is a slot of its own beside it.
  3. Texts in the preview are placeholders: the app writes into the parts named #list-item/…. Nothing hidden.

On the screens now

A list is one slot for all its rows: a frame named #<screen>/<name> (for example #wifi/networks) as wide as a row (size=wide 960, column 490) and as high as the rows it shows, with Clip content on, and inside it as many preview instances of #list-item as fit, one row pitch apart (72 high, 8 between: 80). harry places the real rows at their scrolled position; the preview rows only show the designer the list. The scrollbar is a slot of its own beside the list (#<screen>/<name>-scrollbar, an instance of #scrollbar of the list's height), not inside it.

slot name

harry reports a gesture

The finger is on the node named SLOT: harry hit-tests the drawn tree and hands the app Gesture::Down, moves, Gesture::Up with that name.

actions.rs: one match arm, the component decides

harry's gesture is an action of the app like every other (the listener below sends it). The app's apply matches the node name: you add this arm. The component takes the gesture, updates itself (pressed, on or off, the finger's position) and answers with an event when the gesture completed something, None otherwise.
// the list itself (a drag between rows) or a row, "SLOT/<row>"
_ if node == "SLOT" || node.starts_with("SLOT/") => {
    if let Some(ListEvent::Chosen(row)) = state.list_item.on(row_of("SLOT", node), gesture, Instant::now()) {
        let _ = row; // yours
    }
}
the component's side: pub fn on(&mut self, gesture: Gesture) -> Option<ListItemEvent>
once per app: the listener that turns harry's input into an action (ui_event_listener.rs) 
impl UiEventListener for UiListener {
    fn handle_event(&mut self, event: UserInputEvent) -> HandleEventStatus {
        // everyware_ui::Input groups harry's touch events into Gesture::Down / Move / Up per node
        for (node, gesture) in self.input.feed(&event) {
            let _ = self.actions.send(Actions::CustomAction(HomeAction::Gesture(node, gesture)));
        }
        HandleEventStatus::Consumed
    }
}

state.rs: the component lives in the app's state

One value per place on the screen; it holds what is pressed, chosen, typed. The app owns it, so it survives between frames and the presenter can read it.
use everyware_ui::list_item::{ListItem, ListItemKind};
use everyware_ui::list_view::{ListEvent, ListView};

pub struct State {
    pub list_item: ListView,
}

// in State::new
list_item: ListView::new([ListItem::new(ListItemKind::Plain, "Title", "Supporting text")], 744.0, 72.0 + 8.0),
A list is a ListView of rows (ListItem), its slot interactive; new rows with state.list_item.set_rows(...) keep a tap in progress.

presenter.rs: state → UI model

After every action the presenter writes the component into its slot: variant, texts, opacities, the transition of the last change.
model.list_item = list("SLOT", &state.list_item);

ui_model.rs: what to show, by node name

One field per node in everyware_ui::ui_model! { ... }; the SlotCustomizer turns it into harry's customizations.
list_item: Slot = "SLOT" interactive ["SlotCustomizer"];

harry draws

The clone of the chosen variant in the slot, with the parts set (#list-item/pressed fades in while pressed): the picture on the left is what the device shows.

    let row = node.strip_prefix("#wifi/networks/").and_then(|r| r.parse().ok());
    if let Some(ListEvent::Chosen(row)) = wifi.list.on(row, gesture, Instant::now()) {

kind is what the row carries: plain, icon (a leading glyph), image (a leading picture), toggle, chevron, text (a value on the right, for label and value rows). lines one to three, size the width (regular, column 490 for two columns in a dialog, wide 960). state only default, selected, disabled: pressed is a layer.

Rows do not stand alone on a screen: a ListView (core/src/list_view.rs) holds them, scrolls them (drag, fling, Android's physics), selects one and reports a tap; the slot of the list is a clipping frame with preview rows, harry places the rows at their scrolled y.

What the code sets, and how it moves

the roles of Material 3's list item: #list-item/title (headline), /subtitle (supporting text, not in lines one), #list-item/pressed opacity (pressed): set by code. Slots #list-item/leading (kind icon) and #list-item/trailing (kinds plain, icon): instances of #icon, the glyph set by code, the trailing one shown or hidden. Kind image: #list-item/image (a picture the app registered, set by code) and #list-item/trailing-text. Kind text: a label (#list-item/title) and its value (#list-item/trailing-text, right aligned), lines one only. lines: one and two (72) for the kinds plain, icon, toggle and chevron, two and three (128, headline and supporting text up to two lines each) for image. Rows of a scrolling list (ListView, harry glue list()): a clipping slot, rows pitch apart, drag/fling as Android

Rust API

core/src/list_item.rs

pub enum ListItemKind

The kind property of #list-item: what is at the ends of the row.

PlainText only.
IconAn icon before the text.
ToggleA toggle at the end.
ChevronA chevron at the end: opens something.
ImageAn image before the text (a registered picture, everyware_ui::images) and a trailing text at the end.
TextA label and its value (the trailing supporting text of Material 3) at the end, in one line: "Firmware · 0.1.0".

pub enum ListItemLines

The lines property of #list-item: the height of the row.

OneThe headline only (72, the touch target).
TwoHeadline and one line of supporting text (72).
ThreeHeadline and supporting text up to two lines each (128); with an image only.

pub enum ListItemSize

The size property of #list-item: the width of the row (a variant has a fixed size).

Regular440 wide: a column of a card.
Column490 wide: a column of a dashboard.
Wide960 wide: a sheet's list.

Where it lives, how to change it
Figma#list-item on the Components page (set the file key in the menu)
Specvendor/sdv-everyware/ui-lib/components.json:9 properties, values, transitions
Rustvendor/sdv-everyware/ui-lib/core/src/list_item.rs:69 ListItem, the state machine
harry bindingvendor/sdv-everyware/ui-lib/harry/src/slot.rs:633 the parts of the clone the code sets
  1. A property, a value or a transition: components.json; the order of props is the order of the variant name.
  2. The drawing: the component set #list-item in the Figma library, every variant; the layers the code sets keep their names #list-item/<part>, nothing hidden.
  3. The behaviour: the Rust module (ListItem; variant() produces the set's variant string); the parts: the harry binding.
  4. Fetch the design into the app and run everyware_ui_test: it fails when a variant or a part the code uses is missing in the design.
Traps
  • A glyph per row is not a variant (harry does not swap a variant inside a list item): every glyph of the stack is in the row at opacity 0 and leading(icon) lights one.
  • Rows replaced while a finger is down: set_rows carries pressed and selected over by the row's key, so the tap still lands.
  • The scrollbar is its own slot beside the list; inside the list it would scroll away with the rows.
